{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ3jMp88AAAABXGvzng", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6oxzhAqqnU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6ox", "number": 3, "title": "Upgrade glTF TSL loader/exporter plugins to v0.4.0 (THREE_materials_tsl Draft v2.0)", "body": "## Problem

The editor currently depends on `@takahirox/gltf-three-materials-tsl-exporter@^0.3.0` and `three@^0.182.0`, registers the exporter plugin with a project-local `createDefaultNodeSerializer()`, and loads imported glTF assets using the stock `GLTFLoader` without registering the `THREE_materials_tsl` loader plugin.

The upstream [`THREE_materials_tsl` specification](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl) has moved to **Draft v2.0**. The [exporter](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/exporter) and [loader](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/loader) source packages both declare **v0.4.0** and target this encoding. The new encoding requires the actual NodeMaterial `materialType` and is incompatible with v1.0 by simply changing the `version` field. Upstream v0.4.0 documentation reports validation with Three.js r186 (`three@0.186.1`).

The current editor therefore needs an end-to-end migration so that exported and imported TSL glTF/GLB assets can round-trip using the new packages/specification.

## Expected outcome

Use the latest **published, compatible** loader and exporter packages (target `@takahirox/gltf-three-materials-tsl-loader@0.4.0` and `@takahirox/gltf-three-materials-tsl-exporter@0.4.0`), support `THREE_materials_tsl` Draft v2.0 when importing and exporting, and keep existing ordinary glTF and editor functionality working.

**Publication note:** Both upstream source manifests currently say `0.4.0`. Confirm availability in the npm registry before installation; if publication/registry propagation is still pending, retry after it becomes available rather than substituting an older or unverified package.

## Context and implementation tasks

- [ ] Confirm npm publication and current plugin APIs; update `package.json` and `package-lock.json` to use both compatible v0.4.0 packages, removing obsolete integration if appropriate.
- [ ] Align `three` and `@types/three` to a compatible, tested version (upstream baseline: `three@0.186.1`, `@types/three@0.186.0`), adapting the editor to any relevant Three.js/TSL API changes. Do not assume compatibility with an untested newer Three.js release.
- [ ] Update **both** GLTFExporter usage paths in `src/App.tsx` (glTF text preview and GLB download) to the v0.4.0 `THREEMaterialsTSLExporterPlugin` API. Use the upstream `createDefaultNodeSerializer` where supported; review `src/tslGltfExporter.ts` and retain only project-specific overrides/adapters that are genuinely necessary.
- [ ] Register `THREEMaterialsTSLLoaderPlugin` with `GLTFLoader` in the editor's glTF asset loading path, supplying the required `createDefaultNodeResolver()`. Preserve existing KTX2 loading and geometry/material/texture node behavior. Ensure loaded NodeMaterials are usable in the existing preview/editor flows.
- [ ] Make exports emit **Draft v2.0** (including the correct nonempty `materialType`, graph entrypoints and references) and imports reconstruct supported material types and node graphs. Follow the v0.4.0 plugin API; do not use removed exporter `version` or loader `materialType`/`supportedVersions` options.
- [ ] Preserve ordinary glTF PBR/material extension properties and fallback behavior. Unsupported version (including v1.0 if not deliberately supported), missing material type, invalid graph or unsupported nodes should leave the ordinary glTF material intact rather than partially apply TSL. Route diagnostics through the plugin's `onError` and editor error UI as appropriate.
- [ ] Review any built-in/custom nodes and project serializer/resolver adaptations for v2.0 compatibility. Document unsupported nodes/limitations rather than silently losing node data.
- [ ] Update any affected docs/examples and add reproducible regression coverage for imports, exports and round-trips.

Relevant current files:
- [`package.json`](https://github.com/takahirox/tsl-node-editor/blob/main/package.json)
- [`src/App.tsx`](https://github.com/takahirox/tsl-node-editor/blob/main/src/App.tsx) (exporter registration near lines 15034 and 15212, glTF loading near 15984)
- [`src/tslGltfExporter.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/tsl-node-editor/blob/main/src/tslGltfExporter.ts)

Upstream references:
- [Draft v2.0 specification](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [Loader usage and fallback contract](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/README.md)
- [Exporter usage and serialization limits](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/README.md)

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and `npm run lint` pass with the updated lockfile and compatible Three.js versions.
- [ ] A supported TSL NodeMaterial exported as `.gltf` and `.glb` includes `materials[*].extensions.THREE_materials_tsl.version === "2.0"` and the correct `materialType`, with valid entrypoints/node references.
- [ ] The editor can re-import its exported v2.0 glTF/GLB, reconstruct expected TSL nodes/material types, and successfully preview/re-export them (round-trip). Verify representative Basic, Standard and Physical NodeMaterials, including a shared node graph where applicable.
- [ ] Ordinary glTF/GLB files still import correctly; existing geometry/material/texture nodes, KTX2 assets and non-TSL exports remain functional.
- [ ] Invalid/unsupported TSL extensions fail safely to the ordinary glTF material, preserve supported ordinary material values and produce useful diagnostics; unsupported nodes do not silently produce a misleading successful export.
- [ ] Automated or reproducible fixtures demonstrate the successful round-trip and at least one fallback/error case.

## Optional validation

Manual WebGPU browser visual comparison of the material before export and after import, including a textured/PBR material.

## Required post-merge verification

Because this repo deploys its demo to GitHub Pages, confirm the published editor loads and its glTF import/export flow works after deployment; keep this pending until the actual deployment occurs.
